name: Ron Paul
role: U.S. Representative from Texas (1976-1977, 1979-1985, 1997-2013); Libertarian and Republican presidential candidate
summary: Ron Paul is a libertarian-minded Republican who argues for a strictly limited constitutional government, abolition of the Federal Reserve and the income tax, sound money, and a noninterventionist foreign policy with no entangling alliances. He opposes the drug war, the draft, surveillance and federal involvement in education, health care, marriage and abortion law, preferring individual liberty and state-level decisions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Says a free society would be defended by volunteers and favors a strong constitutional national defense.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: End the Fed argues that the Federal Reserve should be abolished and money left to the market.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Says we should work toward abolishing the income tax and replacing it with nothing.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Asks why government should give permission to marry and wants marriage left to voluntary contracts without state licensing.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Advocates sound money redeemable in gold and silver and market wages by mutual agreement, the opposite of abolishing money and wage labor.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Defends property rights and voluntary contracts, which include renting out property.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Says wages are to be set by mutual agreement between worker and employer.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes abortion as an act of violence against a human life and introduced the Sanctity of Life Act to remove federal court jurisdiction over abortion cases.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Says in a free society land is owned by the people, not the government, and calls government management of land atrocious.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wants to cut military spending and end overseas militarism.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Condemns rising deficits and Keynesian stimulus and says debt-fueled spending cannot go on.

ban-interest.rationale: Treats interest rates as a market price that the Fed should not manipulate.

bound-labor.rationale: States that no one is forced to work and no one is prevented from quitting.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Argues that trade and commerce reduce war and that war comes from the state, central banking and interventionism, not free markets.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Credits freedom, private property and voluntary contracts with generating the wealth of the modern world.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Says laws against pornography, gambling and drinking cannot improve personal morality and that conservatives err by enforcing it by force.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wants the Fed audited and ended and says secret, unaccountable central banking drives the business cycle.

central-planning.rationale: Blames central economic planning through monetary policy and legislative mandates for the crisis and calls for free markets and sound money.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Introduced the American Citizenship Amendment so that no child born in the United States to parents who are not citizens or do not owe permanent allegiance is a citizen; Liberty Defined says the same about children of illegal immigrants.

civil-marriage.rationale: Says any agreement between participants should qualify as a civil contract if desired.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Condemns drone warfare and war that kills innocents.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Calls the United States an aggressive, expansionist empire and condemns invading and occupying other countries; he opposes rule over foreign peoples.

collective-defense.rationale: Endorses the founders' refusal of entangling alliances and objects to going to war under NATO or UN banners.

conscription.rationale: Liberty Defined's chapter on conscription calls the draft involuntary servitude, an outrage never to be tolerated, and says a free society would be defended by volunteers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Complains that money in politics far surpasses productive investment and that government favors special interests, including large corporations.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Says wages are to be set by mutual agreement with no mandates and no special authority for unions or business, and condemns welfarism mixed with corporatism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Says people should not be able to vote to take away the rights of others and that unlimited majority rule is tyranny.

death-penalty.rationale: Says he used to support the death penalty, now does not support the federal death penalty and no longer trusts government to carry it out, yet won't interfere with states that impose it.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: States that dependency on the federal government is worse than at any time in history and sets as his goal unwinding the federal welfare and entitlement system, gradually and without harming current recipients.

decide-locally.rationale: Defends states' rights under the Tenth Amendment as a bulwark against federal power and wants education, marriage and criminal law left to states and localities.

democracy-best.rationale: Holds that democracy's dynamic turns small government into big government and that people should not be able to vote away others' rights; he prefers a constitutional republic.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Condemns Soviet-style communism and every form of government that claims unlimited power over individuals.

direct-action.rationale: Says change will come from a battle of ideas and education, as a peaceful continuation of the American Revolution, and campaigned through elections.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Describes the electoral college as a feature that emphasized state power over central authority and that the founders considered important.

direct-votes.rationale: Prefers a republic in which not everything is subject to mob rule over direct democracy.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Objects to laws that segregate people by race, gender or sexual orientation and to government drawing such distinctions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Says a right to goods like medical care can only be provided at others' expense by force and rejects redistribution.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Argues liberty yields prosperity that is well distributed and that using force to make outcomes fairer is wrong.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Counts himself a global-warming skeptic and doubts that a global body of bureaucrats could plan climate outcomes.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Says patriotism means obedience to the principles of liberty, not to the state, and puts individual rights above collective demands.

economic-freedom.rationale: Holds that freedom, private property and voluntary contracts generate prosperity and that sacrificing economic liberty erodes liberty overall.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Calls trade barriers harmful and favors free trade and travel with all countries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Says terrorism no more justifies suspending due process, habeas corpus or the Second Amendment than it justifies suspending murder laws.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Introduced H.R. 1146, the American Sovereignty Restoration Act, to withdraw the United States from the United Nations, and calls UN authority a transfer of US sovereignty.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Endorses Jefferson's call for peace and commerce with all and entangling alliances with none and says it is time to bring American troops home from around the world.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Says affirmative action laws substitute one violation of individual rights for another and exacerbate conflict.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Insists the Bill of Rights and constitutional principles do not change with the times.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Argues environmentalists would sacrifice liberty and economic progress, and says polluters should answer through property law.

equal-conscription.rationale: Wants an end to the draft and registration for all, 'without age, sex or any other restrictions', so neither sex is drafted.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Argues that all individuals must be treated the same under the law and rejects group-based penalties or privileges.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Says that when economic equality is the goal poverty results and that using force to make the economy fairer is to be rejected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Says hysterical resistance to nuclear power cost the economy trillions and pushed less environmentally friendly alternatives.

experts-over-public.rationale: Writes that government attracts people who think average people need smart people to take care of them and calls this demagoguery.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Calls for ending the drug war and rejects suspension of due process.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Says the country needs a constitutional amendment limiting taxes and spending, as Milton Friedman argued, rather than merely balancing the budget.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Calls the American Civil War ghastly and probably needless and says abolitionists favored secession.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Says a supposed right to medical care can only be guaranteed at others' expense by force.

free-public-college.rationale: Says federal involvement in education has made college costs skyrocket and favors private provision and competition.

free-trade.rationale: Says he favors free trade and diplomacy, and that trade and friendship reduce the chance of war and protective tariffs harm consumers.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Says trade and friendship diminish the chances of war with other nations.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Says private discrimination in associations is a cherished right that should never be regulated and that forced hiring has no place in a free society.

harm-principle.rationale: Holds that physical aggression should be used only defensively and that laws banning adults' use of substances are an intrusion on liberty.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Says plainly that you can count him among the global-warming skeptics.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Calls for ending welfare and entitlement programs.

indirect-election.rationale: Lists the Seventeenth Amendment (direct election of senators) with the Federal Reserve and the income tax as a product of the progressive era's attack on liberty.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Insists that all rights are individual and unrelated to belonging to a group, and objects to talk of group rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Treats opposition to modernity, cars and industry as dangerous and credits economic progress with human welfare.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Says there is no doubt Jews have a historic claim on the land itself, while opposing US aid.

land-redistribution.rationale: Defends private property and condemns forced transfers.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: States that no one is forced to work.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Liberty Defined says to treat all drugs the way alcohol and cigarettes are treated and to decriminalize them; prohibition is incompatible with a free society.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Describes campaign finance reform as an attack on First Amendment political speech and welcomed the ruling striking down McCain-Feingold's limits.

limit-growth.rationale: Calls radical environmentalists who oppose economic progress and modernity creepy and dangerous.

limit-guns.rationale: Liberty Defined's gun chapter says gun control cannot work and clears a path for violence, and that an armed society is a polite society.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues that government or bureaucratic decisions on spending capital are always inferior to private decisions (Liberty Defined, Foreign Aid) and that free-market prices direct resources, while central planning and credit allocation misallocate them (End the Fed).

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: Defends states' Tenth Amendment role and personal nullification of unconstitutional laws against federal power.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Advocates a gold and silver standard and the Constitution's gold and silver legal tender.

more-religion-public.rationale: Says the Constitution does not prohibit religious expression in public places and objects to strict bans on voluntary prayer, while rejecting any official state religion.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Says the Constitution, not the UN or treaty bodies, holds authority and that trade agreements sacrifice national sovereignty.

national-mission.rationale: Calls exporting democracy dangerous and the Iraq and Afghanistan justification of spreading America's goodness a lie.

natural-rulers.rationale: Treats the claim that smart people should rule over average people as demagoguery and holds all individuals equal under law.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Defends the individual's right to own weapons of self-defense and says physical force is justified defensively.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cites approvingly the view that government should be restricted to protecting people and their property and that it may not grant privileges to any class.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted No on the 2008 bailout (H.R. 1424, TARP, roll call 1856).

no-business-privileges.rationale: Calls corporate welfare something he can never support and says government may not grant privileges to particular classes.

no-central-bank.rationale: End the Fed's central thesis is that there should be no central bank.

one-party-rule.rationale: Opposes authoritarianism and bipartisan consensus around bad ideas and holds that no party should direct the state beyond constitutional limits.

open-borders.rationale: Says an ideal libertarian world would have blurred and open borders but that owners would still control entry and that today's conditions, welfare and drug war require rules.

party-controls-media.rationale: Defends free speech and press against control, including informal control through political correctness.

person-over-state.rationale: Says patriotism means supporting the people against the state and that rights belong to individuals.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says all the reforms in the world will not eliminate the corruption in the system and that bailouts reward banking and corporate elites.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Says pollution is unjustified aggression that must be punished or enjoined and that businesses may not socialize their costs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Says WTO, NAFTA and CAFTA sacrifice national sovereignty to international bodies and opposes transferring sovereignty to the UN.

positive-liberty.rationale: Says everyone has a right to pursue medical care without hindrance but no right to have it provided, since that needs forced transfers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Calls wage and price controls bogus government solutions to price problems caused by monetary inflation.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Explains inflation as monetary and says price controls only misdiagnose it.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Says exporting democracy is the most dangerous idea and has led to huge sacrifices of lives and wealth.

property-fundamental.rationale: Names freedom, private property and enforceable voluntary contracts as what generates wealth and warns that insecure property rights undermine other rights.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Treats private property as a fundamental right protecting individuals, not a privilege conditioned on collective good.

public-money-creation.rationale: Wants money created by the market on gold and silver, not by any central body.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Defines racism as defaming a group by race and denying it rights, and notes resentment toward Hispanic immigrants is unfair.

racial-franchise.rationale: Defines racism as denying a group full rights in the civic community and rejects it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Calls the belief that a group trait trumps individual traits the beginning of a racist cast of mind.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Says governments notoriously wrote laws segregating people by race and that such laws violated individual rights.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted No on the 2007 Fair Minimum Wage Act (H.R. 2, passage, roll call 17 of 10 January 2007) and on its recommittal and procedural votes.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposes both closed and open borders, wants border enforcement and an end to welfare for illegal immigrants but a generous guest-worker program and rejects mass deportation; no clear call to cut levels.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Describes the economy as over-regulated, overtaxed and distorted, and wants an end to regulatory privileges for corporations rather than tighter regulation.

religion-illusion.rationale: Defends religious belief as a source of charity and moral order and criticizes atheists for blaming religion for the world's ills.

rent-control.rationale: Calls wage and price controls bogus government solutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Argues that liberty is the source of prosperity and that sacrificing liberty produces neither.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Calls political correctness very close to an infringement of free speech and rejects hate-crime laws as unequal treatment; he consistently defends First Amendment speech.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Lists the war on pornography among the discussion-stifling bugaboos and rejects laws to make people more moral.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Opposes all foreign aid as a taxpayer-funded form of credit allocation and says aid obstructs reform.

right-to-secede.rationale: Told the House he prefers many small independent governments pledged not to aggress, and notes abolitionists favored secession.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Says government should leave marriage out and recognize any voluntary contract, yet personally holds the traditional definition and sponsored the Marriage Protection Act to keep federal courts from forcing states to recognize same-sex marriages.

school-vouchers.rationale: Says vouchers, tax credits and charter schools help only a few and leave the state in control of curriculum, preferring tax credits and homeschooling.

self-ownership.rationale: Asks whether we own our bodies and ourselves and answers that we do.

separate-church-state.rationale: Says the Founders were right to reject an official religion but objects to the modern reading demanding strict removal of public religious expression.

separated-powers.rationale: Laments that separation of powers between state and federal government has virtually disappeared and that power has shifted from Congress to the executive.

social-market-economy.rationale: Favors free markets without state economic direction or social-insurance mandates.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Complains that government operates outside the rule of law and demands strict adherence to constitutional limits.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Rejects gun control and says disarming citizens makes aggression by terrorists or governments more likely.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Says government allocation of capital is always inferior to private allocation and opposes industrial policy and corporate subsidies.

state-harmful.rationale: Wants a drastically smaller, constitutionally limited government (courts, defense, property protection), not no state.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: Opposes plans to tax, regulate and monitor the Internet and says government will cite pornography and crime as excuses.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Favors noninterventionism and no entangling alliances with any power.

strong-leader.rationale: Criticizes the shift of power from Congress to the executive branch and presidential bypassing of Congress on war and spending.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted No on the USA PATRIOT Act reauthorizations (H.R. 3199 in July and December 2005, S. 2271 in March 2006, H.R. 514 in 2011).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberty Defined's chapter on trade policy says protective tariffs harm consumers, breed inefficiency and make war more likely.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted Yes on the death-tax repeal bills (H.R. 8 in 2000 and 2001, H.R. 5638 in 2006).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wants to abolish the income tax and replace it with nothing, so he opposes higher taxes on the wealthy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Says the income tax implies government owns you and endorses the Nozick comparison of taxing earnings to forced labor.

term-limits.rationale: Says he has voted for and supported term limits but does not think they would solve much.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Calls for rejecting the unsustainable cost of policing the world and expanding the American Empire.

total-state.rationale: Rejects state direction of economy, culture and education and calls authoritarianism the enemy of liberty.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Opposes managed trade agreements such as NAFTA, CAFTA and the WTO as not free trade.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Warns that big-government supporters want to prevent private encryption that would guarantee privacy on the Internet and calls for keeping the Internet free and private.

unions-good.rationale: Says the 1935 Wagner Act deepened the Depression and that a free market grants no privileges to unions or business, while allowing workers to organize voluntarily; he is critical of union power rather than hostile to voluntary unions.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Says a free market grants unions no authority or privileges and wages are set by mutual agreement.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Liberty Defined's chapter on medical care rejects a right to medical care, because it can only be guaranteed at others' expense by force and leads to rationing.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Says he supports peaceful civil disobedience to unjust laws with every fiber of his being and calls it personal nullification of unconstitutional laws.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Says welfare benefits and free medical care attract illegal immigration and should not be extended to illegal immigrants.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Holds that all contracts between workers and businesses must be mutually agreeable and without government mandates.

notes: Pilot under the 2026-11-05 rules: every statement in statements.json was answered, candidates included (null where no position was found). Searched: his six books in the local reference corpus (full text searched by keyword and, for Liberty Defined, chapter by chapter), his House floor speeches and extensions of remarks (Congressional Record, GovInfo, local congress corpus), and his House roll calls (local Voteview dataset). Themes searched: economy (taxes, money, Fed, welfare, labor, trade, health, education), government (Constitution, war powers, federalism, executive power, term limits, elections, direct democracy, secession), world (UN, NATO, alliances, aid, sanctions, interventions, trade agreements, Israel), liberty (drugs, guns, surveillance, civil liberties, conscription, speech), society (abortion, marriage, religion in public life, race, discrimination, immigration), ecology (climate, nuclear, pollution), technology (encryption, internet) and means (civil disobedience, revolution, nullification). Where he has a roll-call record on a statement (minimum wage, USA PATRIOT reauthorizations, Iraq 2002, the 2008 bailout, estate-tax repeal) the answer rests on the vote alone and is medium. His mature positions are used: on the death penalty he says his view changed from support to not supporting the federal death penalty. No answer was made from his party, newsletters published under his name, or critics. YouTube was not used. Most society, culture and technology statements concern doctrines on which he has said nothing, so they stay null.
